No. The evidence shows no countable tree-cover loss on this property since the 2020-12-31 baseline.

- The only post-baseline loss is 0.4 ha in 2021, in patches under the 0.5 ha minimum event size. These are not counted as events.
- Hansen data cover the whole property and run through 2025, so the monitoring window is fully observed.
- The larger losses (0.8 ha in 2008, 25.5 ha in 2015, 4.8 ha in 2017, 67.7 ha in 2020) all happened before the baseline. They are history and fall outside your 2021 window.

Context: Hansen shows 23 ha of tree cover in 2000, and the JRC map shows no forest in 2020 (0 ha). So there was little tree cover left to lose by 2021.

One caveat: the MGAP 2021 source was unavailable. The Hansen and JRC datasets were both available, so this does not change the conclusion.
